newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at six-year high on rally hopes.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at six-year high on rally hopes.

text.p: Taiwan share prices surged 1.40 percent on Monday to notch their highest close since June 1990 on hopes for a renewed rally around the February 7 Chinese lunar new year, brokers said.

The weighted TAIEX index gained 100.12 points or 1.40 percent to close at 7,254.32. That surpassed the 7,206.42 point close of January 16, which until Monday had stood as the highest close since 7,339.71 on June 5, 1990.
Turnover was a hectic T$107 billion, the highest since T$125.9 billion recorded on December 3, 1996.
Brokers said Monday's rally was fuelled in part by big lunar year-end bonuses being received by investors.
"This is a so-called 'bonus-driven rally' as inflows of investors' bonuses likely will help push up the index around the Chinese new year," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities.
Brokers said another factor was a shift of money from investors' bank accounts into the market.

"Many investors have diverted some savings to the market, thinking that a share's single-day seven percent limit up already is higher than a whole year's time deposit rate of six percent," said Jardine Fleming fund manager George Hou.
Asset-backed shares rose most, with BES Engineering up T$1.7 to T$32.2 and Imperial Hotel limit up to T$43.4.
Plastics led most of the day's gains on rebounding prices of raw materials, although the upswing eased near the close, rising only 1.95 percent. China Petrochemical was up T$1.6 to T$40.2.
Textiles surged on expectations of strong seasonal sales in the second quarter, with Shinkong Fiber up T$1.4 to T$22.8, brokers said.
Hou cautioned that the rally had turned speculative. "The economic fundamentals, though they are improving, are not strong enough to support the recent rally," he said.
